title.narrative: Strengthening Birth Registration Systems to Protect Every Child from Child Labour

description.narrative:
The overall goal of the project is to increase the rate of birth registration in the three selected model countries, Côte d’Ivoire, Mozambique and Nigeria, by 2024 as a key strategy to combat modern slavery and prevent and respond to violence and exploitation of vulnerable children.
UNICEF will support global and continental initiatives and national efforts in the three countries in Sub-Saharan Africa to increase and accelerate birth registration for all children from birth by strengthening civil registration and child protection systems, government capacity, and community engagement, with the overall aim of protecting children from modern slavery, including child labour, human trafficking and exploitation. Protecting children from child labour requires that every child has access to services that protect them. This means that children have access to education, including quality and relevant learning, that vulnerable households can access social protection programmes to tide over difficulties, and that parents and caregivers have adequate wages and opportunities for decent work.
